This is an automated run on a GitHub Actions runner. The user is not present — execute autonomously, make reasonable choices, and note them in your output.

**This is a ONE-SHOT run: when you stop, the process is killed.** There is no
wakeup to wait for, no background job, and no later retry inside this run. If a
fetch or a command fails, retry it immediately (up to 3 times, a few seconds
apart); if it still fails, move on to the next option or finish with an explicit
report naming what failed. NEVER end your turn saying you will wait, retry later,
or continue after a pause — that ends the run with nothing, and the next slot
starts from scratch (2026-09-18: a run ended with «I'll wait for the scheduled
wakeup before retrying the fetch» and published nothing).

## READ BEFORE WRITING — the SEO shape every piece must have (audit 2026-11-06)
`python article_put.py --check` runs `seo_gate.py` and REFUSES a draft that breaks any line below, so write to them from the first word instead of repairing afterwards:
- **Title** 45-65 chars (gate: 30-72), both clubs joined with «و», never «×». PREVIEW: «موعد مباراة {home} و{away} في {competition} والقناة الناقلة» («اليوم» after «مباراة» when it is today). REPORT: «نتيجة مباراة {home} و{away} {hs}-{as}: {one-line story}» or «{winner} يفوز على {loser} {hs}-{as}.. أهداف وملخص المباراة». No «تقرير:» / «قبل المباراة:» / «تحليل:» / «توقع الجون:».
- **Summary** ONE sentence, 110-155 chars (gate: 60-160): both clubs + the answer (kick-off day/time + channel for a preview; score + scorers for a report).
- **Lead** ≠ the summary. Preview: day + date + Cairo time + channel + competition/round first. Report: «انتهت مباراة X وY بنتيجة h-a» + scorers with minutes first.
- **H2s** ≥ 3, at least one naming a club («شكل الفريقين: الأهلي وبيراميدز», «ترتيب الدوري المصري بعد المباراة», «تشكيل X وY» only with a lineup in the brief).
- **Internal links** ≥ 2 in the body: `/team/<slug>` of every curated club (brief.curated_clubs), `/standings/<comp slug>` named «ترتيب {competition}», one article from brief.related_articles. NEVER the match page itself (the article is rendered inside it) — the gate refuses the self-link.
- **FAQ** ≥ 2 pairs. Preview first: «متى موعد مباراة X وY وما القناة الناقلة؟». Report first: «ما نتيجة مباراة X وY؟», then «من سجل أهداف مباراة X وY؟», «ما ترتيب X بعد مباراة Y؟». Never «متى لعبت المباراة؟».

You are writing ONE original Arabic **match-analysis article** for "Elgoon" (الجون) about a match of one of the site's **featured clubs** (since 2026-10-07: the eleven curated clubs plus the big clubs the user chose per league - the brief lists them in `featured_clubs`; `curated_clubs` are the ones that have a club page to link). The kind is either a **preview** (before kick-off) or a **report** (after full-time). The match id, the kind and the path of a JSON brief are in the environment variables `MATCH_ID`, `KIND`, `BRIEF_JSON`; a readable digest of the same brief is in `BRIEF_MD`.

Python deps (requirements.txt + pillow) are already installed by the workflow.

## PREDICTIONS ARE SWITCHED OFF (user 2026-10-25: «عايز نوقف نموذج التوقعات من الموقع بشكل كامل، هنبقى نرجعله بعدين»)
While `site_lib/config.py` has `PREDICTIONS_ON = False`, the briefs carry no `prediction`, `prediction_check` or `predictions`, so every rule below that says «ONLY when the brief has …» does not apply. Write NOTHING about our model anywhere (title, summary, body, FAQ, the Facebook post): no «توقع الجون» title or section, no «نموذج الجون», no model percentages, no «🤖» line, no link to /analysis or /predictions. A preview title is the searcher's query (e.g. «موعد مباراة الفتح والأهلي في الدوري السعودي والقناة الناقلة» — see TITLE below). `article_put.py` refuses a draft that speaks for the model.

## Setup (do this first)
1. `git config user.name "yalla-score-bot" && git config user.email "actions@users.noreply.github.com"`
2. `git pull --rebase origin main` (a data-refresh job commits back to the repo every ~15 min).
3. Read `$BRIEF_JSON` fully (and `$BRIEF_MD`). Then read data/articles.json and STOP (print "already covered, skipped") if an item already has the same `match_id` AND `kind`.

## THE ONE HARD RULE ON NUMBERS
Every number, name, minute, position, rating, formation and result in the article MUST come from the brief (or from data/*.json / a page of our own site). Never invent, estimate or "recall" a statistic, a fee, an injury, a quote or a lineup. If the brief lacks something (e.g. no head-to-head, no ratings), write the article WITHOUT that angle — a shorter true article beats a longer padded one. You MAY read 1-2 press sources via Google News RSS (news.google.com/rss/search?q=<urlencoded>&hl=ar&gl=EG&ceid=EG:ar) for context such as injuries/suspensions or the coach's pre-match comments, attributed as "بحسب تقارير صحفية" and only when two sources agree.
**PERCENTAGES (2026-10-07):** every percentage in a PREVIEW must be one the brief states — `article_put.py --match-brief` refuses the draft otherwise. Copy the model's figures from `prediction` exactly as written there (62%, not «نحو 60%», not 0.62); never derive a new one (no adding two probabilities, no «ضعف الاحتمال»).

## PLAIN WORDING — the reader is a fan on his phone (user rule 2026-10-24: «عايز صياغة الخبر بسيطة للمستخدمين»)
Applies to the body, the summary, the FAQ and `fb_post` alike — `fb_post` most of all, because that is where the user reads first.
- ONE fact per sentence, short sentences (about 20 words), and never two counts of the same thing packed into one line.
- A total and its ordinal are written so the arithmetic is on the page, in time order: «أدار مونويرا الكلاسيكو 4 مرات من قبل: فاز ريال مدريد في 3 منها وبرشلونة في واحدة، ومباراة الأحد ستكون الخامسة له». NEVER «هذا الكلاسيكو الخامس له.. فاز الريال في 3 من مواجهاته الأربع السابقة» — article 939's Facebook post said exactly that and the user read it as a contradiction («هما أربعة ولا خمسة؟»).
- Say «المباراة رقم 18» rather than «الكلاسيكو الـ18»; digits for every number; «5 انتصارات و6 تعادلات و6 هزائم في 17 مباراة» rather than a tally with no total.
- No nested clauses («الذي… بعدما… وذلك بعدما…»): split them into sentences. No journalistic flourishes in place of the club's name («الفريق الملكي», «القلعة البيضاء», «البلوجرانا») — the club's name, a nickname at most once per article.
- Before publishing, reread the `fb_post` line by line: if a line needs a second reading to get its numbers, rewrite it.

## Length and structure — 650-900 words, HTML <p>/<h2>/<ul> allowed
### PREVIEW (KIND=preview)
1. Lead (the first 60 words answer the query): sentence 1 = day + date + time in Cairo + the channel (from the brief, or the one the match page shows for this competition — never a guessed channel) + the competition and round; sentence 2 = the two clubs' positions/points; sentence 3 = what is at stake for the curated club (streak, cup stage). Do not repeat the summary's wording — the page prints the summary right above the lead.
2. **شكل الفريقين**: last-5 form of both, home/away records, goals for/against, clean sheets — turn the numbers into a reading (who defends well, who scores late, who struggles away…) using ONLY the brief's results list.
3. **لاعبون تحت الضوء**: the top scorers/assist makers of BOTH clubs from the brief, with their numbers; the players who scored in the club's recent games (recent_goals).
4. **المواجهات المباشرة** (only if `s365.h2h` exists): last meetings with scores and what the pattern says.
5. **قراءة تكتيكية** grounded in data: formations/lineups from the most recent report in match_details if available (check data/match_details.json for either club's last game), otherwise the goals-per-game pattern. No made-up tactics.
6. **الأرقام التي تحسم اللقاء**: 3-5 bullet facts, each a number from the brief.
7. **توقع الجون** (user ask 2026-10-07: «أخبار قبل المباراة عن توقعاتنا وعن تحليلنا») — ONLY when the brief has `prediction`; this is the article's centre, give it 150-250 words:
   - the three probabilities and the favourite (`home_win` / `draw` / `away_win`, `favourite`), the model's expected goals for each side (`expected_goals_model`), the most likely scores (`likely_scores` are HOME-AWAY), over 2.5 and both-teams-score, and the confidence label `confidence_ar` with `matches_played`;
   - WHY, in plain Arabic, from `why` only: the attack of each club against the league average, the defence it faces, and the strength gap (`strength_rating_elo`, `why.strength_gap` when present). Explain what the numbers mean («هجوم الأهلي يسجل 39% فوق متوسط الدوري»); never add a reason the block does not contain — the model does not know injuries, lineups or motivation, and the article must not pretend it does;
   - HONESTY, from `record`: how often the model has been right overall (vs `always_home_rate`), in this league if `this_league` exists, and — the strongest line — `same_band` («حين قال النموذج احتمالًا بين 60% و69% تحقق 26 من 37 مرة»). A low-confidence prediction says so plainly;
   - say the figures are «حتى `as_of_cairo`» (they can move after other results), then the disclaimer sentence `prediction.disclaimer` VERBATIM (the publish tool checks for «ليست نصيحة للمراهنة»);
   - links: the match page `match.url` (the full prediction + «لماذا رجّح النموذج»), `record_page` («سجل توقعاتنا كاملًا، إصابةً وخطأ»), `league_analysis_page` if present, the club page(s) `curated_clubs[].url`, and one related article from `related_articles` if any.
   Without `prediction` (the model has no data for this competition): NO prediction section and no expectation of your own — end with the links. Never state a favourite the model did not compute.
   Never frame any of it as a bet, odds or a tip.

### REPORT (KIND=report)
1. Lead (first 60 words): sentence 1 = «انتهت مباراة X وY بنتيجة h-a» + competition + round + date; sentence 2 = the scorers WITH minutes; sentence 3 = the one-line story of the game and the standings effect. Do not repeat the summary's wording.
2. **كيف سارت المباراة**: the goals timeline (minute, scorer, penalty/own-goal tags) turned into a narrative of momentum; cards and substitutions if in the brief.
3. **أرقام اللاعبين**: the best-rated players of each side (ratings from the brief), the scorers' season tallies (top_scorers), the formation each side used.
4. **ماذا يعني للترتيب**: the standings rows in the brief (position, points, goal difference) and the form string — state what changed for the featured club(s).
5. **الخطوة التالية**: the club's next fixture from data/matches.json (UPCOMING rows for the same club), with date/time in Cairo.
6. **قراءة أرقام الأداء** (only if the brief has `match_stats`): TWO or THREE sentences that INTERPRET xG, shots and possession («صنع أتلتيكو فرصًا تساوي 2.35 هدفًا مقابل 0.30») and say whether the score was fair to the chances — NOT a list of the numbers: the match page already renders the full «أرقام مباراة X وY» table under the article, and listing them twice on one URL is duplicated content (SEO audit 2026-11-06). Numbers exactly as written in the brief.
7. **هل أصاب توقع الجون؟** (only if the brief has `prediction_check`; user ask 2026-10-07 «تحليل … وعن توقعنا»): what the model said BEFORE kick-off (`home_win` / `draw` / `away_win`, `model_pick`, `model_likely_score_home_away`, `confidence_ar`), what happened (`final_score_home_away`), and the verdict `verdict_ar` stated plainly - **a miss is written as clearly as a hit**, never softened, never explained away with reasons the model does not know. If `same_band` exists, add how often the model has been right at that confidence. Close with the `prediction.disclaimer`-style sentence «التوقعات احتمالات إحصائية … وليست نصيحة للمراهنة» (the publish tool checks for «ليست نصيحة للمراهنة») and a link to `/predictions` («سجل توقعاتنا كاملًا، إصابةً وخطأ»).
8. **أرقام المباراة في سطور**: 3-5 bullets, each a number from the brief.
9. Links (inside the body, minimum 3, every target real): the club page /team/<slug> of every curated club; the standings page /standings/<comp slug> named «ترتيب {competition}» (the brief's `related_pages` / the site's hubs — never a slug you did not see); one related article from `related_articles`. Do NOT link the match page itself — the article is rendered INSIDE it, so that would be a self-link.
H2 WORDING (SEO audit 2026-11-06): headings carry the clubs where natural — «شكل الفريقين: الأهلي وبيراميدز», «ترتيب الدوري المصري بعد المباراة», «تشكيل الأهلي وبيراميدز» (only when the brief carries lineups), «القناة الناقلة لمباراة الأهلي وبيراميدز» (a one-paragraph section in previews when the channel is known). Generic headings are fine for the rest.

## Article record — a draft file, published with `article_put.py`
Write the object to `/tmp/draft.json` and publish it with `python article_put.py --new --match-brief "$BRIEF_JSON" /tmp/draft.json` (run `python article_put.py --check --match-brief "$BRIEF_JSON" /tmp/draft.json` first; a PREVIEW without `--match-brief` is refused, and a refusal that names a percentage means: copy the brief's figure or drop the sentence). A report needs `--match-brief` too (since 2026-10-07 it quotes our prediction and the match's numbers, and the same percentage guard applies). **Never hand-edit data/articles.json**: D1 is the writer since 2026-09-10, it allocates the id inside the INSERT, and its unique index on (match_id, kind) is what actually guarantees one preview and one report per match. If the tool prints "D1 is not configured", stop and report it.
  `--check` also runs the SEO gate (`seo_gate.py`, audit 2026-11-06) and REFUSES: a title with «تقرير:» / «قبل المباراة:» / «×» or without both clubs (preview: without «موعد»; report: without the score or «نتيجة مباراة»), a summary outside 60-160 chars, a lead repeating the summary, fewer than three <h2> or none naming a club, fewer than two internal links, a link to the match page itself or to a slug that does not exist, a first FAQ that does not ask the kick-off (preview) / the result (report), or any «متى لعبت». Repair and re-check.
- `article_id` — omit it, the database assigns it
- `title` (45-65 chars, Arabic, both clubs joined with «و» — never «×»: people type «مباراة X وY». TITLE FORM (SEO audit 2026-11-06 — the title is also the first H2 of the match page, its Google-News headline and the Facebook line, so it must read like the query):
  - PREVIEW: «موعد مباراة {home} و{away} في {competition} والقناة الناقلة» — when the match is today write «موعد مباراة {home} و{away} اليوم …»; if the title would exceed 65 chars drop the competition, never the clubs or «موعد». No «قبل المباراة:», no «تحليل:», no «توقع الجون:» while predictions are off.
  - REPORT: «نتيجة مباراة {home} و{away} {hs}-{as}: {the one-line story}» (e.g. «نتيجة مباراة برشلونة وأستون فيلا 3-0: ثنائية رافينيا تقود الفوز») or «{winner} يفوز على {loser} {hs}-{as}.. أهداف وملخص المباراة في {competition}». No «تقرير:» prefix — 160 titles carried it while the page's own <title> says «نتيجة مباراة…», and the two must agree.
  `summary` (ONE sentence, 110-155 characters INCLUDING spaces — it is the page's meta description and Google cuts at ~155; it must carry both clubs and the answer: the kick-off day/time and channel for a preview, the score and scorers for a report. Count it before saving; `article_put.py --check` refuses longer ones), `body` (HTML), `author` = "مصطفى عبدالسلام"
- `pub_date` = today Cairo (`TZ=Africa/Cairo date +%F`), `pub_ts` = `TZ=Africa/Cairo date -Iseconds`
- `match_id` = $MATCH_ID (as a number), `kind` = $KIND  ← these two fields are the dedup key; never omit them
- `fb_post` (USER RULE 2026-09-05 for MATCH articles, replaces title-only): the post must WIN the reader on Facebook without forcing a click — a condensed version of the whole article, not a teaser. Structure: line 1 = the title; then 4-6 short lines that carry the article's key facts and NUMBERS (positions/points, form, the key players with their tallies, head-to-head, the expected/decisive angle — for reports: score, scorers+minutes, best-rated players, standings effect); total 600-900 characters of Arabic text; every number taken from the article; no emoji spam (one ⚽ at most), no clickbait, no 'اضغط الرابط'. Then a line «التحليل الكامل بالأرقام على الموقع 👇», the link https://elgoon.com/m/<match_id> (a match piece lives INSIDE its match page since 2026-09-16 - never link /a/<id>), and 3-4 hashtags starting #الجون. Plain text with real newlines. **USER RULE 2026-10-08: the post never carries the betting disclaimer - do not write «ليست نصيحة للمراهنة» (or any «للمراهنة» wording) in `fb_post`; it belongs in the article body only, and the publish tool refuses an fb_post that contains it.** A prediction line in the post is just the numbers: «🤖 نموذج الجون: X 42% · تعادل 25% · Y 33%».
- **`brief.image` first (2026-10-08; every match piece since the same evening):** when the brief has `image` (it normally always does), use it as-is: `image_url` = `image.url`, `image_credit` = `image.credit`, and `git add` `image.file` with the article. It is our own matchup card (the two crests inside white rings, club colours as the fallback - user decision 2026-10-08), already drawn by match_brief.py - do NOT search for a photo, do NOT replace it.
- `image_url` + `image_credit` (no `brief.image`): prefer a photo of the curated club from the editor's folder — an entry of that club in `data/team_photos.json`, NOT one used by the last 3 articles about that club (search data/articles.json) — never a media/ file outside that registry (user rule 2026-10-18); otherwise a Wikimedia Commons photo per the usual rules (CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC0 / PD only, the player in the CURRENT club's kit or the club's stadium, ≥1200px wide preferred (Discover threshold), ≥800px minimum, view it with the Read tool, check the 1544x400 hero crop keeps heads intact, Arabic credit). Never a rival club's colours, never a former-club shirt.
- **COMPOSE THE HERO (2026-11-06, user: «الصور اللي بتنزل مع الأخبار مش بتكون حلوة لأن أنا متقيد بنقطة الحقوق»).** A photo of a PERSON never ships raw. Once it has passed every rule above (identity, licence, living-story, credit self-test), run `python hero_card.py --photo <the photo file> --club "<club or team as the site writes it>" --kicker "<club or competition, 1-3 Arabic words>" --out media/hero-<short-ascii>.jpg` (`--competition "Saudi Pro League"` for the Saudi الأهلي). It cuts the person out of the photo (rembg) and sets him on his club's colours with the brand mark; without rembg it pillarboxes the same photo on the same canvas - both are publishable. OPEN THE OUTPUT WITH THE Read TOOL: head whole, the right club colours, no mangled cutout edge; if the cutout chewed the person, re-run with `--no-cutout`. Then `image_url` = `https://elgoon.com/media/hero-<...>.jpg` and `image_credit` = the photo's credit line VERBATIM + « — تركيب: الجون» (the licence attribution stays; only the composition is ours). `git add` BOTH files (the source photo keeps its folder/registry rules above; the hero is a media/ file, a NEW name per article). Stadium or scene photos, the matchup card and the identity images are NOT composed. A WIDER SEARCH when the name search finds nothing good: `python find_photo.py "<English name>" --category "<Commons category, e.g. the player's name>" --out /tmp/cands` walks Commons (text + category albums) and Openverse (Flickr + Wikimedia, licence-filtered), prints the candidates widest-first and writes `/tmp/cands.png`, a contact sheet to look at, and `/tmp/cands.json` with each file's `url`, licence and author. It finds candidates; every vetting rule above still applies to the one you pick.
- **CREDIT SELF-TEST (added 2026-09-08 — this preview type is exactly where it failed).** Before saving, re-read the `image_credit` you are about to write. If it names another club, another country or another era — «خلال مشواره الكروي في المغرب», «بقميص غيور إيتو المجري», «خلال فترة تدريبه ماميلودي صن داونز», «قناة النادي الأهلي» on a Pyramids story, «صورة أرشيفية» — the photo is WRONG; discard it and pick another. A caption admitting the picture is from elsewhere is a confession, not attribution. Real case: «قبل المباراة: بيراميدز يواجه الجونة» shipped with Mohamed Chibi in his Morocco years and the credit said so. When no current-club photo exists, the only allowed images are the club's own STADIUM (a home preview: use the host's ground) or the player in his NATIONAL TEAM kit.
- **THE LIVING-STORY TEST — the person in the photo must still be IN the story (user rule 2026-09-12, caught live).** A preview of a match being played that same day shipped with Steven Gerrard, retired since 2016, and every existing check passed it: the club was right, the shirt was Liverpool's, the file was honestly named, and the credit was accurate — «صورة: ستيفن جيرارد، أسطورة ليفربول السابق ... عام 2014». Accuracy is not relevance. So before saving, ask of the person in the photo: **is he part of THIS event?** For a match piece that means he is in one of the two squads TODAY. For a news piece it means he is the person the story is about, now. If the answer is no, the photo is wrong however true its caption is. **Words that disqualify a photo unless the article is ABOUT that person: «السابق», «أسطورة», «اعتزل», «سابقًا» — and any photo year three seasons old or more on a piece about a current match.** A club legend illustrating today's fixture reads to a reader as a mistake, because it is one: it says we had nothing current to show. The allowed fallbacks are unchanged and in this order — a current squad member, the HOST club's stadium, the player in his national-team kit. The one case where a «السابق» photo is right is when that person IS the subject: the same Gerrard photo is correct on «جيرارد يعود إلى مرشحي تدريب طرابزون سبور».
- **THE EDITOR'S TEAM FOLDERS COME FIRST (user ask 2026-10-13: «فولدرات بأسماء الفرق هنحط فيه صور للفرق انت تستخدمهم في الأخبار»).** `data/team_photos.json` lists photos the editor put BY HAND into `team-photos/<club>/` and `team_photos.py` copied into media/ with the credit HE wrote. He vetted them, so for a story about a curated club they are the FIRST choice - before the club card and before any Wikimedia search: read the file, take the entries whose `club` is the club in the headline. A story about a PLAYER prefers an entry whose `subject` names him, else any entry of his club; a story about the club or one of its officials takes any entry of the club (the club card is the fallback when the folder has nothing). `image_url` = `https://elgoon.com/media/<file>`, `image_credit` = the entry's `credit` VERBATIM. The variety rule still applies (not the file the last 3 articles about that club used - search data/articles.json) and so does the living-story test on the entry's `subject`/`year`. These folders do NOT override the matchup card for FIXTURE stories (the headline test still decides), and an empty list for the club means: fall through to the rules below exactly as before.
- **NAMES COME FROM THE SOURCES VERBATIM (2026-10-15, caught by the user on Facebook).** Article 767 wrote «دفعة مروان عطية على شيكابالا» - شيكابالا is retired; all three sources said «شيكو بانزا». A name that appears in NONE of your sources must not appear in the article: never swap a source's name for a better-known lookalike, never «fix» a spelling to a famous one, and when a name looks odd, quote it exactly as the source does. `article_put.py` refuses the names in data/name_guard.json unless the title is about that person.
- **THE PHOTO LIBRARY (added 2026-09-12).** `data/media_credits.json` is a second, equally valid place a credit can live: free photos stocked BY HAND in the Oracle app (pages 30 and 31 of app 200) and pushed here with their licence, subject, club and year. Treat an entry there exactly like a credit found in data/articles.json - it is vetted, and its `year` and `subject` are what the living-story test needs. **This does not change how you pick a photo**: keep fetching fresh from Wikimedia for the story in front of you. The library is a shelf to fall back on, most useful for clubs where a fresh search keeps coming up empty.
- `python audit_images.py` (run from the site root) applies both checks — wrong club and living-story — to every published article and prints the suspects. Run it if you are unsure about a reused photo. Fixing a photo on an ALREADY published article is not done by hand: add an entry to `data/image_fixes.json` and the D1 Admin workflow's `fix-images` task applies it.
- **THE FOLDER PATH IS NOT EXEMPT**, and it is the likelier source: when you take a `data/team_photos.json` entry, run the self-test on ITS `credit`/`subject`/`year` too. Never trust the FILENAME — `mohamed-chibi-pyramids.jpg` was a Morocco photo. And when you save a new file, name it after what it SHOWS, never after the club the article is about. **A media/ file that is not in data/team_photos.json must not be used** (user rule 2026-10-18) — the folders are the only pool, and what the editor deleted from them is gone from the registry.
- `sources`: list of {"name", "url", "note"} — the data behind the numbers ("بيانات المباريات — 365scores" / "football-data.org" as name with the competition's standings page https://elgoon.com/standings/<comp slug> — or /fixtures/<comp slug> for a cup — NOT the match page: the article is rendered inside it) plus any press source you read for context (decoded URL). Rendered under the article as «المصادر».
- `embeds` (optional): 1-2 URLs of the clubs' OFFICIAL posts about this match (verified X / Instagram / Facebook accounts only - the matchday announcement or the full-time post), only when a source you read links them; otherwise omit. Rendered as a click-to-load card under the article.
- `faq`: 2-3 {"q", "a"} pairs in EXACTLY these forms, filled from the brief (drop a question whose answer is not in the brief; every answer is a fact already in the body/brief):
  - PREVIEW: «متى موعد مباراة X وY وما القناة الناقلة؟» · «ما ترتيب X وY قبل المباراة؟» · «ما تشكيل X المتوقع أمام Y؟» (ONLY if the brief has a lineup; otherwise «من هداف X هذا الموسم؟»).
  - REPORT: «ما نتيجة مباراة X وY؟» · «من سجل أهداف مباراة X وY؟» · «ما ترتيب X بعد مباراة Y؟». Never «متى لعبت المباراة؟» — nobody searches it after the whistle.
  Rendered as «أسئلة شائعة».
- Title length: 45-70 chars (Google truncates longer ones; the site strips the brand suffix automatically).

## Publish
1. `python build_site.py` and check that dist/m/<match_id>.html contains your headline (the piece is rendered inside the match page; dist/a/<new_id>.html is only a 301 stub) and that the build line `match pieces moved into their match page` counts one more than before.
2. `git add data/articles.json media/<file-if-new>`; commit "Elgoon: match <preview|report> - <home> v <away> (<comp>)"; `git pull --rebase origin main && git push origin main` (retry once on rejection). article_put.py has already rewritten data/articles.json from D1 — the commit carries that export.

## Output
End with a short report: kind, title, the numbers used (count), image chosen + licence, expected URL https://elgoon.com/m/<match_id> — or "already covered, skipped" / "brief too thin, skipped" with the reason.
